messages:
incident-bot: paging alert — runtime-r3 (us-west-2a) reporting sustained GPU paging and a brief OOM spike at 2780000000. metrics: GPU memory writeback high, page faults increased 6x. Impact: ~12% of generation requests returning 500s. Paging mitigation -> on-call. :rotating_light:
Elaine: I’m on it, grabbing logs and checking which model shards are affected. switching the node to maintenance mode for new requests.
Sam: ETA? customer-facing slack already flagged elevated 500s for a single customer org.
Elaine: ~2m to gather logs + start a mitigation. putting a short note in support.
DevOps-Jordan: If this is KV-cache related fragmentation, we might see heavy per-batch allocations. Can you paste `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY` and the runtime logs?
Elaine: pasting snippets: ```
> nvidia-smi -i 1 --query-gpu=memory.total,memory.used,memory.free --format=csv
memory.total [MiB], memory.used [MiB], memory.free [MiB]
16160 MiB, 15072 MiB, 1088 MiB
```
Recent dmesg shows repeated page faults and `gpu_mem_swap: triggered`. Runtime logs show repeated `alloc_gpu_pages(size=...)` failures.
Ash: Looks like fragmentation: free memory small chunks but total low. Which model and batch sizes on that node?
Elaine: Affected model: open-redwood-v1-7b (quantized) shard set 3. Typical batch_size=8 for this route.
Sam: Can we lower batch_size for that route to 2/3 as a quick mitigation? That reduces peak working set.
DevOps-Jordan: We can hot-route new requests to another pool but capacity is tight. Quick config change: lower batch_size and reduce max_concurrent_requests to throttle warm-up. I'll push a canary change to runtime-r3.
SRE-Jen: Also consider aggressive KV-cache prefix eviction on that node — evict older entries and shrink per-request cache. That helped in previous fragment events.
Mike: I can run an in-place reduction: `curl -X POST https://internal-api/configs/runtime-r3 -d '{"batch_size":3,"max_concurrency":64}'` — should I go ahead?
Elaine: Do it. Before/after metrics and a tail of runtime logs please.
Mike: Executed, response 200. Applying KV eviction command: `./kvtool evict --node runtime-r3 --policy lru --percent 30` (started).
Elaine: Logs after change (tail): ```
[2780000125] runtime: reduced batch target -> 3
[2780000140] kvcache: started eviction 30% LRU
[2780000180] gpu: page fault rate -> dropping from 6x to ~1.4x
[2780000200] allocation: success after eviction
```
DevOps-Jordan: Nice — page faults trending down. Any 500s still?
Customer-Impact-Bot: Current impact: 500 rates from runtime-r3 reduced from 12% to 2% over last 10m. Affected customers: org-phi (major), org-echo (minor).
Sam: Good. We should still do a controlled restart of the runtime after business hours for full defrag. For now the hot fix is OK.
Ash: Hypothesis tracking: (1) KV-cache fragmentation caused by variable-length kv entries + long-lived prefixes, leading to unusable small free slots; (2) larger-than-average batch causing transient allocation spikes; (3) potential kernel cuda driver churn. Priority: 1 then 2.
Elaine: Adding timeline entries: root OOM spike 2780000000, mitigation start 2780000040, config change 2780000105, eviction kicked 2780000112, stabilization observed 2780000180.
SRE-Jen: Can someone upload a full heapmap and the per-segment free list snapshot to the incident channel? We need for RCA. Use `runtime-dump --heapmap /tmp/heapmap-278000.dmp` and upload.
Mike: Uploading heapmap now -> https://artifacts.internal/heapmaps/heapmap-278000.dmp (private link). Also uploaded `kv-index-278000.log` and `nvidia-stats-278000.log`.
Sam: Customer comms: support to send an update to org-phi with mitigation and ETA for the scheduled restart. I'll draft.
Elaine: Draft ack: "We're aware of elevated 500s earlier today due to GPU memory fragmentation on a runtime shard. We've reduced batch sizes and evicted cache entries to mitigate; full restart scheduled at 02:00 UTC for lasting fix. No model weights changed. We'll follow up after post-restart verification." Thoughts?
Sam: LGTM. Add note about possible transient shorter latencies during restart window.
DevOps-Jordan: Next steps for RCA: analyze heapmap to see free-run fragmentation pattern, correlate per-request allocation sizes from request logs, check for a KV eviction bug that might leave tiny unusable slabs. Assign: Ash + Jen to dig into heapmap, Elaine + Mike to reproduce in staging with same traffic pattern.
Ash: Will run a stress harness that emits the same distribution of sequence lengths and batch sizes.
SRE-Jen: I'll annotate the timeline and create the incident doc skeleton. Will include mitigations, timeline, heapmap snapshots, and proposed long-term fixes: compaction routine for KV cache, cap on per-request contiguous allocations, and a runtime-level small-block allocator.
Customer-Impact-Bot: Final impact summary draft: "~12% error rate for 18 minutes, primary impacted org: org-phi (approx 3% of their requests), mitigation applied reduced errors to ~2%. No data loss reported."
Elaine: Closing actions: create follow-up ticket for compaction and runtime allocator, schedule restart for 02:00 UTC, and postmortem meeting tomorrow 10:00 UTC. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Sam: Thanks, everyone.
Elaine: marking channel resolved for now — will update post-restart.
